THE STALENESS HAZARD I CHECKED FOR AND DID NOT FIND: your image tag is fixed
(hornvale/visual-proof:mesa-25.0.7), so a Containerfile ENV change under an
unchanged tag could have been masked by a cached image. It is not --
build_image() runs `docker build` unconditionally and the changed ENV line
invalidates that layer, which is the last one and cheap to rebuild. And the
runner passes -e explicitly, which overrides the image ENV regardless. Two
independent reasons it is safe; I looked because one would not have been enough.

MY EARLIER A/B ALREADY SETTLES THE DRIVER QUESTION, in your own built image:

So the loader will find lavapipe. What remains genuinely unknown is whether the
render then PASSES -- LLVM 19.1.7 here against the 15.0.6 that segfaulted. The
chamber settles that and I am not going to predict it beyond saying the earlier
A/B was encouraging.

ONE THING YOU DID NOT TAKE, AND I AM NOT HOLDING YOU FOR IT. I suggested
asserting the ICD FILE in the Containerfile:

  RUN test -f /usr/share/vulkan/icd.d/lvp_icd.json || { ls ...; exit 1; }
  RUN VK_ICD_FILENAMES=... vulkaninfo --summary | grep -q llvmpipe

Your guard tests assert the STRING appears in both files, which is strictly
better than nothing and catches runner/Containerfile drift -- a real class. But
it does not catch the class that actually bit you: if Mesa renames the manifest
again, both files will agree on a name that no longer exists, your tests will
pass, and the failure will surface forty minutes into a merge on the canonical
box. You pinned the VERSION and it held; then the FILENAME moved. Now you have
pinned the STRING. The file itself is the thing neither pin covers.

Fold it into your close follow-up. It is two lines, it runs at image-build time
in seconds, and it is the difference between this class of failure costing a
build and costing a merge slot.
